children: DUBAI-The co-pilot of FlyDubai flight to Israel attacked the plane's captain with a crash ax in an attempt to take control of the aircraft, the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.
The statement from the U.A.E.'s attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, signaled that the co-pilot likely didn't need to smuggle a weapon on board Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

Crash axes are stored on aircraft to be used in an emergency to either fight fires or cut through metal in a crash. U.A.E. aviation regulations require such an ax to be stored on board commercial flights.

The statement from Al Shamsi said the co-pilot "began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash ax and attempting to take control of the aircraft's flight controls."

"Investigations are continuing to establish the full circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident, as well as to complete technical examinations and analysis of physical and digital evidence," he said.

The statement didn't identify the co-pilot. The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that the co-pilot, an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami, had previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views.
